item.title: Partial Breakdown of Integrability in Nearly Integrable Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the persistence of integrable structures in real-analytic nearly integrable systems under perturbations that may destroy some, but not all, of these structures. Specifically, we establish upper bounds on the numbers of real-analytic first integrals -- quantities conserved by the motion -- and commuting vector fields -- infinitesimal generators of continuous symmetries -- that can persist under the perturbation. These bounds are expressed in terms of Melnikov-type functions, which quantify the breakdown of the corresponding integrable structures. Unlike classical Melnikov theory, our conditions occur even in the absence of zeros of the Melnikov functions, so they do not necessarily imply the existence of homoclinic tangles. We give a geometric interpretation of these conditions in the context of the Arnold diffusion problem, showing that they imply micro-diffusion. We also obtain a criterion for higher-dimensional nearly integrable systems in which the dimension of the span of the Melnikov vectors restricts the numbers of possible first integrals and commuting vector fields. This shows that the geometry of the Melnikov vectors provides a new mechanism for detecting the breakdown of integrability. We give several applications to integrable Hamiltonian systems subject to forcing and dissipation.
item.dc:creator: Marian Gidea, Shoya Motonaga

item.title: New criteria for upper bounds on the number of limit cycles in Li\'enard systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study upper bounds for isolated periodic orbits of generalized Li\'enard systems on a single potential well. Common-curvature and common-intercept conditions yield uniqueness and hyperbolicity, while a convex--concave condition on the potential-profile slopes gives an upper bound of two. The statements allow finite unequal potential endpoints; appropriate versions also admit degenerate restoring forces and reduced regularity. We prove a uniqueness extension across slope interfaces, a quantitative joint weak-damping criterion, and a compensation criterion controlled by two derivatives. A separate response comparison at neutral cycles, combined with a connected parameter-family argument, gives a coefficient criterion for a two-cycle bound. Applications include classical quartic systems, negative-parameter and positive-parameter Selkov systems, a uniqueness conjecture for arbitrary-degree polynomial systems, and explicit smooth and nonsmooth examples. Existence is proved separately whenever an exact count is asserted. Restrictions to a potential well, a parameter region, or a compact width interval are retained throughout.
item.dc:creator: Chen Cao, Hebai Chen, Yilei Tang

item.title: A smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres with Bernoulli geodesic flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.30464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.
item.dc:creator: Keith Burns, Tomas Gedeon, Yuping Ruan

item.title: When Language Models Misinterpret Uncertainty in Earth System Mechanism Attribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.30501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanistic attribution in Earth system science requires quantifying uncertainty and communicating its implications. Here, we develop an uncertainty-aware mechanistic attribution pipeline that constructs probabilistic fingerprints from ensemble estimates, including covariance-aware separation of competing mechanisms, and an evidence ladder that systematically varies the information provided to language models (LLMs). We evaluate this framework in an idealized stochastic system and a coupled El Ni\~no model using controlled interventions and ensemble data assimilation. In the idealized system, numerical separation increases GPT-4o's intervention-label agreement from 0.80 to 0.98, but not GPT-4o-mini's. In the coupled system, both LLMs identify seven of eight fingerprint-ambiguous events when given full fingerprints with verbal interpretations; GPT-4o's false ambiguity reports decrease from 10/82 to 1/82, without consistent gains in intervention-label agreement. For eight historical ENSO events, the uncertainty-aware condition agrees with the model-inferred mechanism labels in seven cases. These findings distinguish uncertainty assessment from its communication.
item.dc:creator: Pouria Behnoudfar, Nan Chen

item.title: Return Time Sets of Minimal Points for Countable Group Actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a countably infinite discrete group $G$, we study subsets of $G$ that contain a neighbourhood return-time set of a minimal point in a $G$-flow $X$. For $e\in F\subseteq G$, we characterize this property by the existence of $e\in A\subseteq F$ such that $\operatorname{Int}_K(A):=\{t\in G:Kt\subseteq A\}$ is right syndetic for every finite $K\subseteq A$, and equivalently by the support of a minimal binary configuration in the Bernoulli shift $2^G$. Additional conditions on $\operatorname{Int}_K(A) \operatorname{Int}_K(A)^{-1}$ characterize realization by minimal flows that are weakly mixing of all finite orders or strongly mixing: for every such $K$, the former requires that for each finite $H\subseteq G$ there is $c\in G$ with $HcH\subseteq \operatorname{Int}_K(A) \operatorname{Int}_K(A) ^{-1}$, whereas the latter requires that $\operatorname{Int}_K(A)\operatorname{Int}_K(A)^{-1}$ be cofinite. We also construct, for every compact metrizable minimal $G$-flow, a free minimal, strongly mixing Cantor flow disjoint from it.
item.dc:creator: Jian Li, Yini Yang

item.title: Collinear motions in constant curvature spaces, and coplanar motions in $\mathbb{R^4}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.30567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A collinear motion of an $n$-body problem is one in which the $n$-bodies always lie along some, possibly moving, geodesic during their evolution. We prove that every collinear motion of $n\geq 3$ bodies in a constant non-zero curvature space is necessarily contained in some fixed constant curvature space of dimension at most three. For natural systems admitting energy and angular momentum integrals, we further show that every such motion is necessarily a relative equilibrium: evolving under uniform rotation while maintaining constant mutual distances. These results extend certain classical results on collinear motions in Euclidean spaces, initiated by P. Pizzetti, to general spaces of constant curvature. The same methods also yield a partial answer to a question of A. Wintner. Namely, we show that any concave and always coplanar motion in the Euclidean 4-body problem, where the moving plane containing the bodies sweeps out an $\mathbb{R}^4$, must be self-similar: maintaining constant mutual distance ratios over the motion.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Barrera-Anzaldo, Abimael Bengochea, Connor Jackman, Ernesto P\'erez-Chavela

item.title: Pluripotency and Anosov Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.30636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two notions of pluripotency for dynamical systems. Strong pluripotency refers to the possibility of reprogramming, by arbitrarily small perturbations, the forward orbits of points in a set of positive Riemannian volume so that they track a prescribed orbit in a uniform time-averaged sense. In contrast, pluripotency, also called ``statistical pluripotency" in this paper, requires only asymptotic agreement of empirical measures. Strong pluripotency implies statistical pluripotency, but the converse need not hold. For $C^r$ transitive Anosov diffeomorphisms, $r\ge2$, we prove that strong pluripotency fails for every nonempty reference set. On the other hand, statistical pluripotency holds for a nonempty reference set if and only if it is contained in the basin of the unique SRB measure. This basin is invariant and has full Riemannian volume, but contains no periodic points. These results reveal a sharp distinction between the two notions even within uniformly hyperbolic dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Shin Kiriki, Xiaolong Li, Kodai Yamamoto

item.title: On $C^2$ circle diffeomorphisms with rotation numbers of constant type
item.description: arXiv:2610.30750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every irrational rotation number $\alpha$ of constant type and every $q>1$, we construct a $C^2$ circle diffeomorphism $F$ arbitrarily close to the rigid rotation $R_\alpha$ in the combined $C^2$ and $B^2_{2,q}$ topology whose normalized conjugacy is not Lipschitz. We also prove that $F''\in B^0_{2,1}$ implies global $C^1$ conjugacy. Thus the thresholds in the Besov summability and weak Dini scales are $q=1$ and $\gamma=1/2$, respectively. These results complement Herman's Baire category theorem on the residual existence of $C^2$ diffeomorphisms without $C^1$ conjugacy by providing quantitative counterexamples and sufficient conditions for differentiable conjugacy.
item.dc:creator: Junhao Li, Lin Wang

item.title: Reflection symmetry in the equal-mass $1+N$ coorbital problem for $5\leq N\leq8$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study reflection symmetry in the equal-mass Newtonian \(1+N\) coorbital problem for \(N=5,6,7,8\). We prove that every collision-free solution of the angular central-configuration equations has a reflection axis. As a consequence, every non-coalescent limit of planar central configurations consisting of one dominant mass and \(N\) equal small masses is reflection-symmetric about a line through the dominant body. Our proof combines analytic arguments with rigorous computer-assisted verification. For each possible reflection, we introduce variables that measure the deviation from that reflection and vanish exactly when the configuration has that symmetry. The central-configuration equations yield a symmetric matrix equation in these variables. Concavity of the force derivative and estimates of the resulting quadratic forms reduce the symmetry problem to finitely many rigorously verified inequalities. Although the details depend on \(N\), the same general method applies in all four cases. We also obtain, as a separate result, the complete three-class classification for \(N=5\), up to the natural equivalences.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoxiang Huangfu, Zijian Meng

item.title: The Keller-Segel Model for Chemotaxis on Metapopulation Graphs and Graphons
item.description: arXiv:2610.31049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many models of spatial populations use directed motion towards environmental attractants as a mechanism for spatial pattern formation. While prior approaches typically focus on partial differential equation models for directed motion in continuous space, it is natural to consider the dynamics of biological and social systems on a metapopulation featuring well-mixed local patches and spatial motion between patches. In this paper, we formulate a version of the Keller-Segel model for chemotaxis on a graph metapopulation, modeling a chemoattractant that can diffuse across patches and a population of individuals who move through a biased random walk through comparing chemoattractant levels along edges of the metapopulation network. We also derive a continuum limit for our model describing chemotaxis in a population on patches connected by a graphon, showing that our resulting integro-differential equation model arises as the limit of our discrete patch model for families of large deterministic or random graphs. Through linear stability analysis, we derive conditions on the chemotactic sensitivity required to produce instability of a spatially uniform equilibrium for our Keller-Segel models in terms of the reaction parameters and the eigenvalues of the Laplacian operator for the metapopulation graph or graphon. Through a mix of weakly nonlinear stability analysis, numerical simulations, and analytical bounds on solutions, we can also characterize the form of pattern-forming instability in our graphon model and show how our choice of demographic dynamics for the population and the graphon adjacency function can impact the long-time total population size and chemoattractant concentration achieved in emergent spatial patterns.
item.dc:creator: Daecheol Kim, Yefei Zhang, Yuxuan Zhao, Daniel B. Cooney

item.title: Wandering exposed Julia components of rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.31055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every wandering exposed Julia component of a rational map is a point. Here a Julia component is exposed if it meets the boundary of a Fatou domain. The theorem extends the corresponding result for polynomials to rational maps, without any assumption on critical recurrence. The proof combines an enhanced nest with a covering estimate for multiply connected pullback domains.
item.dc:creator: Jinsong Zeng

item.title: Ledrappier-Young entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms with dominated splitting Part 3: full formula with arbitrary multiplicities
item.description: arXiv:2610.31086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the full Ledrappier-Young entropy formula for ergodic invariant measures of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms when the positive Oseledets bundles and their nonpositive complement form a dominated splitting. We prove transverse formulas under three-block domination and equality of metric and unstable entropy under positive-nonpositive domination. To complete the proof, we develop a new mechanism for estimating partial entropy through comparisons of conditional information along orbits. Applications characterize vanishing transverse dimension, give upper pointwise dimension bounds and exact dimensionality of hyperbolic measures. In the quasi-isometric-center setting, this implies a $C^1$ invariance principle for measures with nonpositive center Lyapunov exponents.
item.dc:creator: Yao Tong

item.title: Open dynamics with a moving hole: inhomogeneous IFS and exponential separation condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.31128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal F=\{f_i(x)=r_i x+t_i\}_{i=0}^{b-1}$ be a self-similar iterated function system (IFS) on $\mathbb R$ with $b\ge 3$, and let $K_{\mathcal F}$ be the associated self-similar set. Given $m\in\mathbb N$, for any sequence $\omega=\omega^0\omega^1\ldots$ with each $\omega^i\in \{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^m$ a block of length $m$, let \[ K_{\mathcal F}^\omega:=\pi_{\mathcal F}\left(\{(d_i)\in \{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^{\mathbb N}: d_{k+1}d_{k+2}\ldots d_{k+m}\ne\omega^k\quad\forall k\ge 0\}\right), \] where $\pi_{\mathcal F}$ is the natural coding map from $\{0,1,\ldots,b-1\}^{\mathbb N}$ to $K_{\mathcal F}$. The set $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$ is called the survivor set of an open dynamical system with a moving hole related to $\omega$. When $\mathcal F$ is a homogeneous IFS satisfying the open set condition (OSC), the dimensions of $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$ were determined by the first author, Sun and Wang (Adv. Math., 2026). In this paper we generalize these results to inhomogeneous IFSs. When $\mathcal F$ satisfies the OSC, we give explicit formulae for the dimensions of $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$. In particular, we show that the packing dimension and upper box-counting dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$ always coincide, while the Hausdorff dimension and lower box-counting dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^{\omega}$ are not necessarily equal, which is different from the homogeneous case. Furthermore, when $\mathcal F$ satisfies the exponential separation condition and the similarity dimension $s_{\mathcal F}\le 1$, we are able to determine the Hausdorff dimension of $K_{\mathcal F}^\omega$. Finally, we apply our results to badly approximable numbers and non-recurrence points in the setting of inhomogeneous IFS satisfying the OSC.
item.dc:creator: Derong Kong, Kun Li, Cai-Yun Ma, K\'{a}roly Simon

item.title: Typical periodic optimization and freezing phase transition: Dini potentials and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.31327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the Typical Periodic Optimization (TPO) Conjecture and freezing phase transitions for Dini potentials and beyond. We show that the TPO conjecture fails already at Dini regularity. We identify a sharp regularity threshold for freezing phase transitions, which we call weak log-log Dini. Both results reveal the stability of aperiodic ground states. Moreover, we identify Dini regularity as the sharp threshold for a quantitatitve analog of the freezing phase transition.
item.dc:creator: Yunping Jiang, Zhiqiang Li, Yiqing Sun

item.title: Random Survivor Sets with Moving Holes in Bedford-McMullen Carpets
item.description: arXiv:2610.31440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $2\le m < n$ be integers, and let $K(\mathcal{A})$ be the Bedford--McMullen carpet generated by $\{(x,y)\mapsto((x+i)/m,(y+j)/n):(i,j)\in\mathcal{A}\}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is a subset of $\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\times\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $\mathcal{B}$ for the set of occupied columns, and assume that $\#\mathcal{B}\ge2$ and each column contains at least two symbols of $\mathcal{A}$. At each vertex of the column tree $\mathcal{B}^*$, we independently choose one forbidden symbol from $\mathcal{A}$ according to a prescribed distribution. Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the resulting product measure on $\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. This gives a random survivor set $K_\omega(\mathcal{A})$ with $\omega\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. We show that, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega$, \begin{equation*} \dim_H K_\omega(\mathcal{A})=\frac{1}{\log m}\log\left(\int \sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\ell_b(\omega)^{\frac{\log m}{\log n}} d\mathbb{P}(\omega)\right), \end{equation*} where $\ell_b(\omega)$ is the number of surviving symbols in column $b$ at the root.
item.dc:creator: Derong Kong, Cai-Yun Ma, K\'{a}roly Simon

item.title: Polytopal substitutions and conformal dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.31530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce polytopal substitutions, a recursive procedure for constructing polyhedral approximations of self-similar topological spaces. For a class of substitutions called sub-hyperbolic, we show that the limit of these approximations is naturally homeomorphic to the limit space of the associated iterated monodromy group. We establish a relationship between the $\ell^p$-contraction coefficients of sub-hyperbolic substitutions and the conformal dimension of their limit spaces. In particular, we characterize the conformal dimension in terms of asymptotic moduli and relate these moduli to $p$-energies of graphs.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Nekrashevych

item.title: Continuous-time analysis and algorithms for linear and convex quadratic programs via exactly solvable differential inclusions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Linear and convex quadratic programs are fundamental problems in optimization. While many methods have been developed for solving these programs in large-scale applications, to our knowledge none have attempted to solve their continuous-time gradient flow, a differential inclusion, in full generality without assumptions beyond feasibility. Recent work solved the gradient flows in two special cases, basis pursuit and the lasso, and obtained competitive algorithms. Motivated by these results, we solve the general case exactly. Using the minimal selection principle for monotone differential inclusions, we show that the trajectory of the gradient flow consists of finitely many pieces, each obtained from one nonnegative least-squares problem. Its final piece yields an optimal solution or a certificate of unboundedness. This analysis leads to two algorithms. The first algorithm is exact, terminates after finitely many steps, and applies to linear programs and projections onto polyhedra. The second algorithm, which we call minimal selection descent, discretizes the gradient flow for general convex quadratic programs. Its iterates converge to an optimal solution when one exists and otherwise certify unboundedness. We apply both algorithms to a positivity-preserving limiter for a discontinuous Galerkin scheme and to optimal control problems for the Poisson and heat equations. In the limiter, the first algorithm conserves the total mass more accurately than the state-of-the-art Douglas--Rachford splitting method. On the control problems, minimal selection descent reaches the optimal value to machine precision and is competitive in time with commercial and open-source solvers.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel P. Langlois, Akwum Onwunta, J\'er\^ome Darbon

item.title: Optimal CLT error bounds in the second order Wasserstein metric via Stein's method for weakly dependent sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.30352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use Stein's method to prove general upper bounds on the second order Wasserstein distance in the CLT for general dependent partial sums $S_N=X_1+\ldots +X_N$. Then we use these estimates to provide optimal $O(N^{-1/2})$ rates for a variety of chaotic dynamical systems and $\phi$- and $\psi$-mixing sequences. Our results for $\psi$-mixing sequences are obtained under the fourth moment condition, which matches the best known results in the iid case. This is the first time that optimal CLT rates of any kind are obtained for unbounded weakly stationary variables under general mixing conditions. We then apply this result and obtain optimal CLT rates $O\left((\text{Var}(S_N))^{-1/2}\right)$ for non-stationary $\psi$-mixing sequences without any growth rates on $\text{Var}(S_N)$. We also obtain close to optimal CLT rates for nonconventional sums and some classes of random dynamical systems with non-uniform decay of correlations
item.dc:creator: Yeor Hafouta, Juho Leppanen

item.title: Global Convergence of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a self-contained proof that, for a finite detailed balanced mass-action system with positive rate constants, each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains exactly one positive equilibrium and every positive trajectory converges to it, together with a Lean 4 formalization of the complete argument from persistence to convergence. Boundedness and persistence come from the barrier argument of OpenAI (2026) for weakly reversible systems: an arbitrary-tolerance affine approximation yields a finite-minimum barrier whose superlevel sets confine trajectories and give one logarithmic bound for all solutions from a given initial state. The Horn-Jackson dissipation identity identifies the positive equilibria as an exponential family with parameters in the orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric subspace, which gives uniqueness in each class. A bounded-speed descent argument replaces LaSalle's invariance principle; it uses neither uniqueness of solutions nor continuous dependence on initial data, and it places every cluster point in that family. The route given here is direct and elementary, and its main theorem is checked by the Lean kernel against explicit definitions. The proofs, the Lean development, and the manuscript were produced in ClawsGO Science, an agent harness that packages a complete research environment: Claude Opus 5.5 made the research decisions, GPT 6 Astra carried them out, and the Lean kernel checked every formal step.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Lv (BitMiracle AI Lab), Chengjin Ni (BitMiracle AI Lab), Manqin Wang (BitMiracle AI Lab), Shenli He (BitMiracle AI Lab)

item.title: From Turing Patterns to Spike Self-Replication and Nucleation in a Growing-Domain Tulip Breaking Virus Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.30855v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A recently proposed reaction-diffusion model for the tulip breaking virus (TBV) has been shown to generate striped pigmentation patterns on growing tulip petals. In this paper, we investigate the formation of localized spike patterns in this model in the asymptotic limit of small viral diffusivity. It is known that two distinct bifurcation mechanisms can occur which generate new spikes as the domain half-length $L$ slowly increases: spike self-replication and spike nucleation. Self-replication occurs through a saddle-node bifurcation of the inner spike core problem, whereas nucleation is associated with a fold of the nonlinear outer problem. Using matched asymptotic expansions, we derive critical conditions for these mechanisms and construct phase diagrams that predict which mechanism occurs first as $L$ increases, or whether nucleation is absent. We further combine these results with a Turing instability analysis of the homogeneous steady state to obtain a phase diagram of pattern-forming mechanisms. An interesting finding is that, for the TBV model, the Turing-unstable region lies entirely within the parameter regime where spike nucleation is possible. These results provide further insight into the mechanisms underlying the formation and evolution of pigmentation patterns in virus-infected tulips.
item.dc:creator: Fanya Xia, Chunyi Gai

item.title: Landfall Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.30993v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the negative gradient flow of analytic maps $f:X\to\R$ defined on compact analytic Riemannian manifolds without imposing any nondegeneracy or transversality assumptions. We construct tight isolating blocks around the connected components of the critical set $\Crit(f)$ and record only bounded-time contacts made after an orbit exits one block and before it makes landfall within the interior of another. These contacts assemble into a strict topological category $\cL$ -- called the landfall category -- whose classifying space $B\cL$ is shown to be simple homotopy equivalent to $X$ naturally over all down-sets of the flow partial order. The filtered homotopy type is independent of the isolating blocks. Passing to a finite subanalytic triangulation yields a flow-induced acyclic partial matching, and hence, an explicit finite chain complex generated by the non-exit simplices of the blocks which computes the homology of $X$. The finite model also computes the Morse--Conley spectral sequence over arbitrary coefficients; over a field, homological perturbation further produces a connection matrix whose entries are finite sums over descending contact itineraries.
item.dc:creator: Frances Kirwan, Vidit Nanda

item.title: Sparse power spectrum for passive scalars under Pierrehumbert flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.31241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the long-time Fourier distribution of driven passive scalars transported by an incompressible alternating shear flow (the Pierrehumbert flow) subjected to IID random phase shifts, in the regime of strong shear-strength. With a novel and self-contained proof, we establish (i) a quantitative version of the cumulative Batchelor's law; (ii) quantitative negative regularity mixing estimates; and (iii) a strong form of `sparsity' -- unevenness in the distribution of Fourier mass in radial sectors in frequency space. Our method uses the strong shear-strength assumption to handle a purely deterministic scalar driving term.
item.dc:creator: Alex Blumenthal, William Cooperman

item.title: Model Predictive Control of Wind Turbines: A Model-Oriented Review of Prediction Models, Control Objectives, and Nonlinear Aerodynamic Formulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31295v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has been applied to wind-turbine regulation with markedly different internal prediction models, ranging from linearized low-order turbine models to nonlinear, aeroelastic, floating, and data-driven predictors. This review organizes the literature primarily by the model propagated by the controller and treats model order, predictor representation, MPC formulation, control objective, and validation plant as separate descriptors. Primary studies show that low-order linear or piecewise-affine predictors are attractive for constrained power and speed regulation, whereas flexible drivetrain, structural, and floating models are needed when drivetrain twist, tower motion, blade loads, or platform dynamics are explicit control quantities. Nonlinear and economic MPC studies further demonstrate coordinated pitch/torque control across broad operating regions, while preview, repetitive, and data-driven formulations address wind prediction, periodic loads, and model mismatch. Particular attention is given to aerodynamic pitch dependence: variable-pitch turbine dynamics can be non-affine with respect to applied pitch, and the term NMPC alone does not prove that the original nonlinear pitch map is retained inside the optimizer. The review therefore adopts a conservative, equation-based classification for direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation. Here, direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation means that the applied pitch at each prediction step is evaluated inside the original nonlinear aerodynamic map, rather than replacing that dependence by a linearized, scheduled, piecewise-affine, or learned surrogate. The literature supports a remaining integration challenge at the intersection of flexible drivetrain prediction, nonlinear aerodynamic pitch treatment, explicit constraints and load objectives, and validated adaptive or learned model correction.
item.dc:creator: Roya Khalili-Amirabadi, Mohsen Jalaeian-Farimani, Mahdi Ghane

item.title: Control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This monograph presents a selection of the author's recent works on the control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems. After a detailed introduction to topics related to time-delay systems covered in the monograph, its main contents are presented in a series of mostly independent chapters.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme Mazanti

item.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions I: Algebra, geometry, and a spin model
item.description: arXiv:2610.31485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a family of five-dimensional non-flexible quadratic real algebras $\{\mathcal A_\gamma\}_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}$ with canonical basis $1,i,j,k,\ell$, in which $\gamma$ changes the multiplication but not their norm, and study how this change affects geometry and dynamics. The algebras are pairwise non-isomorphic, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra, and $\mathcal A_1$ is the Pentarnion algebra. The alternating part of the trilinear form $\langle u\times_\gamma v,w\rangle$ induced by the multiplication of $\mathcal{A}_\gamma$ defines a three-dimensional subspace $H_\gamma\subset\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{i,j,k,\ell\}$, tilted by the angle $\arctan(\gamma/\sqrt3)$, whose rotation group $G_\gamma\cong\mathrm{SO}(3)$ contains the automorphism group of $\mathcal A_\gamma$. For $\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2$ the groups $G_{\gamma_1}$ and $G_{\gamma_2}$ generate $\mathrm{SO}(V)\cong\mathrm{SO}(4)$. For the six ways of ordering and bracketing the product of $i,p,p$ in $\mathcal A_\gamma$, two map the unit circle in ${\rm span}\{j,k\}$ to a point and, for $\gamma>0$, four map it to ellipses. As an application, we derive a Hamiltonian model of a classical spin on $H_\gamma$ whose multiplication-induced quadratic energy is isotropic for $\gamma=0$ and anisotropic for $\gamma>0$. It conserves spin length and, for fixed $\gamma$, energy, and satisfies an exact work identity when $\gamma$ varies in time. Numerical experiments with periodically varying $\gamma$ indicate both regular and irregular spin dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Poshtkohi, Susanne Pumpluen

item.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.31600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood. Recent perspectives interpret attention blocks as interacting particle systems, whose mean-field limits correspond to gradient flows of energy functionals on spaces of probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with Wasserstein-type metrics. We extend this viewpoint by deriving accelerated attention blocks from inertial, Nesterov-type damped Hamiltonian dynamics on these density spaces, developing the geometry and differential calculus needed to make the construction rigorous. In particular, we introduce a local-mobility geometry for the Otto-Wasserstein and softmax-Wasserstein settings, and a quotient Stein geometry that resolves the degeneracy of the linear-attention kernel to yield a well-defined metric and differential calculus. We provide rigorous foundations when softmax attention admits a gradient-flow formulation and when its inertial counterpart admits a damped Hamiltonian on explicitly characterized domains. For linear attention, we obtain a finite-dimensional solution theory with sharp conditions for global existence versus finite-time second-moment blow-up. We further prove a quantitative link between continuous moment blow-up and the discrete-layer depth at which token norms cross a prescribed threshold. Finally, motivated by the finite-token geometry, we propose geometric corrections to token and momentum updates. In decoder-only, nanoGPT-style experiments on TinyStories and OpenWebText, these corrections lower validation negative log-likelihood on next-token prediction relative to momentum-only controls.
item.dc:creator: Viktor Stein, Levin Maier, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl

item.title: Restricted variational principle for Lyapunov exponents of typical one-step cocycles
item.description: arXiv:2301.01721v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the multifractal formalism for Lyapunov exponents of typical one-step cocycles. We establish a variational relation between the Legendre transform of topological pressure of the generalized singular value function and measure-theoretic entropies. As a consequence, we show that the restricted variational principle of Lyapunov exponents holds for typical one-step cocycles. Furthermore, we prove a variational principle formula for the generalized singular value function.
item.dc:creator: Reza Mohammadpour

item.title: Conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states on uniformly hyperbolic sets
item.description: arXiv:2506.15503v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states for H\"older potentials on uniformly hyperbolic sets. While standard stochastic stability characterises measures on attractors, we analyse the statistics of transient dynamics on non-attracting sets by conditioning small random perturbations of the dynamics to not escape from our regions of interest. We prove that as the noise intensity vanishes, the quasi-ergodic measure of the $e^\phi$-weighted process generated by $\e$-small random perturbations of the deterministic dynamics converges to the unique equilibrium state associated with the potential $\phi - \log \left|\det \left. D T\right|_{E^u}\right|$. The results are obtained via perturbative spectral analysis of transfer operators acting on anisotropic Banach spaces and topological hyperbolic dynamics arguments. Furthermore, we extend this framework globally to Axiom A diffeomorphisms with multiple basic sets using dynamical filtrations. This work provides a rigorous characterisation of natural measures on uniformly hyperbolic repellers, which are fundamental in the context of transient chaos. Our results have been formalised in Lean~4.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Bassols Cornudella, Matheus M. Castro

item.title: Convergence of the Birkhoff spectrum for nonintegrable observables
item.description: arXiv:2506.21390v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider interval maps with countably many full branches and observables with polynomial tails. We show that the Birkhoff spectrum is real analytic and that its convergence to the Hausdorff dimension of the repeller is governed by the polynomial tail exponent. This result extends previous work by Arima on more regular observables and demonstrates how the tail behaviour influences the structure of the Birkhoff spectrum. Our proof relies on techniques from thermodynamic formalism and tail estimates for the observable and our applications are to natural observations on Gauss maps, L\"uroth transformations as well as to a the first return time for a class of induced Manneville-Pomeau maps.
item.dc:creator: Godofredo Iommi, Mike Todd, Boyuan Zhao

item.title: Extremal Lyapunov exponents in random and simultaneous dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2507.16764v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this manuscript, we consider finitely many maps, all of which are defined on a compact probability space, with at least one map in the collection having degree strictly bigger than 1. Working with two different, however related, dynamics generated by this setting, we obtain an expression for the extremal Lyapunov exponents, that characterise the instability of typical orbits, as the limit of the averages of the logarithm of the operator norm of linear cocycles of generic orbits. We obtain this as a consequence to the Kingman's ergodic theorem for a subadditive sequence of measurable functions, which naturally generalises the Birkhoff's ergodic theorem, in each of the cases.
item.dc:creator: Thirupathi Perumal, Shrihari Sridharan

item.title: Dynamics of Interfaces in the Two-Dimensional Wave-Pinning Model
item.description: arXiv:2601.04746v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the mass-conserved reaction-diffusion system known as the wave-pinning model, which serves as a minimal framework for describing cell polarity. In this model, the interplay between reaction kinetics and slow diffusion forms a sharp interface that partitions the domain into high- and low-concentration regions. We perform a detailed asymptotic analysis and derive higher-order approximation equations governing the motion of this interface. Our results show that on a fast timescale, the interface evolves via propagating front dynamics, whereas on a slow timescale, it evolves as an area-preserving mean curvature flow. Furthermore, using the derived free boundary problem, we demonstrate that on a significantly slower timescale, an interface whose endpoints lie on the domain boundary drifts along the boundary toward regions of higher curvature. In summary, our analysis reveals that the interface dynamics in the wave-pinning model exhibit a hierarchy of three distinct timescales: wave propagation on a fast timescale, curvature-driven area-preserving evolution on a slow timescale, and motion along the boundary on a significantly slower timescale.
item.dc:creator: Shunsuke Kobayashi, Koya Sakakibara, Taikei Uechi

item.title: Selberg and Brolin on value distribution of complex dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2602.08454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Brolin-Lyubich-Freire--Lopes--Ma\~n\'e equidistribution theorem for iterated preimages of a given non-exceptional value and Lyubich's periodic point version of it are foundational in the study of dynamics of rational functions of degree more than one on the complex projective line, and Drasin and the author studied a quantification of the former in a formalism of Nevanlinna theory, or more specifically, with the aid of Selberg's theorem from covering theory. In this paper, we point out that the argument in that previous study has already yielded a better quantification of the Brolin-Lyubich-Freire--Lopes--Ma\~n\'e equidistribution theorem, and also point out that a similar argument also yields a quantification of Lyubich's theorem under an exponentwise version of the so called hypothesis H, which has recently been settled by Przytycki for unicritical polynomials. As an application, we sharpen the quantitative results on the value distribution of the (first) derivatives of iterated polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Y\^usuke Okuyama

item.title: Integer Cantor Sets: Arithmetic Combinatorial Properties
item.description: arXiv:2602.15292v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cantor sets of integers have a rich set of arithmetic combinatorial properties. We consider classical Cantor sets, with a base and a fixed set of allowed digits. For such sets, we (a) give examples of such sets that satisfy the intersective property with power savings (b) characterize uniform distribution, (c) establish polynomial mean ergodic theorems and (d) study metric pair correlation of Cantor sets.
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, Michael T. Lacey, Dario Mena, Maria Carmen Reguera

item.title: Thermodynamic formalism for singular flows
item.description: arXiv:2604.26936v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that $C^\infty$ smooth three-dimensional flows with positive topological entropy admit only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy, even in the presence of singularities (zero-velocity points). Furthermore, for flows in a $C^\infty$-open and dense subset of the space of such three-dimensional flows, every ergodic measure of maximal entropy is rapidly mixing. To prove this result, we construct a novel symbolic coding framework for singular flows, which serves as the fundamental technical tool. We then introduce the property of strong positive recurrence (SPR) for singular flows, and prove that SPR flows can be coded by suspension flows over SPR countable discrete symbolic systems. Under appropriate conditions, we further establish that such suspension flows are rapidly mixing. These frameworks can be further generalized to a broad class of flows, including star flows, and the results naturally extend to general equilibrium states.
item.dc:creator: Ming Li, Xingzhong Liu

item.title: Geometric Properties of Higher Dimensional Solenoidal Attractors
item.dc:creator: Daniele Galli, Eleonora Passaglia, Andrea Ulliana

item.title: Measure rigidity for regular polynomial endomorphisms and applications
item.description: arXiv:2608.23749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^k$ with the same equilibrium measure under some mild condition on the dynamics at infinity. In particular, for $f$ in a Zariski dense open subset of the parameter space and any $g$ of the same degree, $\mu_g=\mu_f$ if and only if $f=g$. We also establish finiteness results for maps with a prescribed equilibrium measure. Our approach rests on the stable manifold structure near the hyperplane at infinity. Applications include a Tits-type alternative, results on iterated centralizers, and an arithmetic non-density theorem.
item.dc:creator: Yugang Zhang

item.title: Extended dynamic mode decomposition with Fourier dictionaries: Error bounds and fast implementation
item.description: arXiv:2609.20144v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Koopman operator has gained considerable attention in dynamical systems due to its capability to provide a linear viewpoint for nonlinear systems using data-driven methods such as extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD). In this work, we propose an EDMD-variant with a Fourier dictionary on the $d$-dimensional torus, where the data are sampled on an equispaced tensor grid. We show that the EDMD regression problem admits a unique closed-form solution and coincides with trigonometric interpolation of the Koopman image. This identification has two consequences. First, using Koopman invariance of Sobolev spaces, we transfer approximation-theoretic results for trigonometric interpolation to derive $L^p$-error bounds, $2 \le p \le \infty$, on approximations of the Koopman operator. In particular, the established bounds are of optimal order with explicit constants. Second, the EDMD matrix never has to be assembled, since its action reduces to (nonequispaced) fast Fourier transforms such that the EDMD-approximation can be evaluated matrix-free with quasi-linear cost in the dictionary size. We illustrate the results for the Kuramoto model of coupled oscillators and for the chaotic ABC flow with dictionaries of up to $10^7$ modes.
item.dc:creator: Felix Bartel, Sandra Ritter, Manuel Schaller, Karl Worthmann

item.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
item.description: arXiv:2609.28059v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$, introduced by Kamae, Widmer and Zamboni, of infinite words $\alpha \in \mathbb{A}^{\mathbb{N}_{0}}$ over finite alphabets $\mathbb{A}$. For recurrent aperiodic words, we determine a lower bound and prove its sharpness. We further give a structural characterization of the words with minimal Abelian maximal pattern complexity. In the general case, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every $k.$ For aperiodic words over $\ell \geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq (\ell -1)(k-\ell +2)$, for all $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell -1)k}+O_{\ell }(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, at every $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset \mathbb{N}_{0}$ for which the bipartite graph on two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_{0}$, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$, is a forest.
item.dc:creator: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng

item.title: A min-max gap characterization of minimal foliations on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2605.12428v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend an energy introduced by Mather to the setting of Almgren-Pitts min-max theory and obtain a parametric, higher-dimensional analogue of Mather's variational barrier theory for twist maps and geodesics on tori. We use this energy to establish several criteria for the existence of foliations of the $n$-torus by minimal hypersurfaces. We show that for a generic metric, whenever a lamination by area-minimizing hypersurfaces of the $n$-torus contains a gap, there exists a minimal hypersurface inside the gap that is not area-minimizing. This hypersurface is a higher-dimensional analogue of the secondary minimax orbit appearing in Aubry-Mather theory.
item.dc:creator: Hoan Nguyen

item.title: Robustness Verification of an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle-based Plankton Classifier
item.description: arXiv:2607.04453v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The assessment of planktonic standing stocks and microorganism structures is critical for understanding upper ocean biological processes. Currently, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) equipped with in-situ optical imaging and artificial intelligence (AI) methods offer a promising solution for persistent surveillance, mapping and monitoring of planktonic life. However, current AI methods often lack robustness in dynamic, unstructured environments, where environmental noise and non-biological artifacts lead to frequent misclassifications. Standard convolutional neural network (CNN) classifiers often struggle with such conditions, leading to misclassifications that require time-consuming manual validation by marine biologists. To address this issue, we propose a novel robustness verification framework for in-situ plankton classifiers based on reachability analysis. We also introduce a continuous-time neural ordinary differential equation (neural ODE) classification model leveraging the high-resolution imaging capabilities of the SilCam particle imager. In this paper, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework by formally verifying the robustness of the neural ODE model against environmental perturbations. We demonstrate that our verification framework acts as an automated filter providing formal guarantees of model stability against ambiguous data, thereby improving the reliability of autonomous sampling and reducing the post-processing workload.
item.dc:creator: Abdelrahman Sayed Sayed, Pierre-Jean Meyer, Asgeir J. S{\o}rensen, Mohamed Ghazel

item.title: Positive-measure intersections of Bedford-McMullen carpets under similitudes
item.description: arXiv:2610.09277v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K=K(n,m,\Gamma)$ be a Bedford-McMullen carpet with $n>m\geq2$ and $1<\#\Gamma<nm$, and let $\mu$ be a self-affine measure on $K$ with strictly positive weights. We prove that every similitude $f(z)=rOz+a$ satisfying $\mu(K\cap f(K))>0$ has a diagonal or anti-diagonal orthogonal part $O$, without any arithmetic restrictions on the defining bases. Under the same intersection hypothesis, we also show that $r\in n^{\mathbb{Q}}\cup m^{\mathbb{Q}}$ whenever $K$ is not a segment. For isometries satisfying this hypothesis, we further prove that $f(K)$ is simply a translate of $K$, thereby establishing a strengthened form of the 2010 conjecture of Elekes, Keleti and M\'ath\'e in this planar self-affine context.
item.dc:creator: Ding-Kun Hu, Huo-Jun Ruan, Jian-Ci Xiao
